liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Reviewer calls Jerry's performance in this song fantastic [27]
- **Samson & Delilah** (1 review): Reviewer believes this is the best version of the song they have seen [27]
- **Ship of Fools** (1 review): Jerry leaned into the wind during this song, steering the audience with perfect bends [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-12-17.nak300.andrewf.131309.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 174 min [1]
- **gd1986-12-17.148871.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 174 min [3]
- **gd1986-12-17.141036.Senn.Hessberg.Miller.Noel.t-flac1644**: source not stated; 24 songs; 174 min [6]
- **gd1986-12-17.sbd.miller.77410.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 178 min; rated 3.57/5 by 14 [13]. Said about its sound: Reviewer states the sound quality is better than their live position at the venue; Recording has skips and sound inconsistencies, though other copies might be better [28][32]
- **gd1986-12-17.nak300.damico.88926.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 178 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [23]. Said about its sound: Recording has slight hiss but clear vocals, well-captured for post-coma 1986 performances [33]

## Around the show

- Third night after Jerry's death scare; band remembered words and played without missing notes [29]
- Metalhead friend bought ten-dollar tickets; crowd was large but not aggressive near the stage [31]
- Babatunde Olatunji joined for the Drums to Jam transition [1]
- Entire ensemble cast joins for a jam from Drums before Space begins [6]
- Sikuru Adepoju on talking drum and Jose Lorenzo on berimbau join the performance [7]
- Second set length matches the July 7, 1986 show, the last before Jerry's coma [26]
- Described as the finest of the three welcome-back shows, with high energy [30]
- This show is the third of three historically significant December 1986 performances [34]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-12-17.nak300.andrewf.131309.flac1644**: taped by Andrew F.; transferred by Andrew F.; source: OTS AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > patched thru one D5 > Sony TC-D5M > Sony ES-Metal 90's, with no Dolby. [1]. Also: MAC from the lead deck provides patches for He's Gone and Throwing Stones [1]
- **gd1986-12-17.148871.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; Neumann KM84i mics > Sony D5M [3]. Also: Schoeps CMC4 MK41 source supplies patches for He's Gone and most of Drums [3]
- **gd1986-12-17.141036.Senn.Hessberg.Miller.Noel.t-flac1644**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: Michael Hessberg Recording: Sennheiser ME80 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M); Charlie Miller DSD [6]. Also: Source 80996 from Suraci and Beckham supplies the start of When Push Comes to Shove [6]
- **gd1986-12-17.sbd.miller.77410.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/TDK MX-XG90) D [13]
- **gd1986-12-17.nak300.damico.88926.flac16**: taped by Joe D'Amico; transferred by Joe D'Amico; source: nak 300 mics w/cp4 shotguns > sony d-5 > mac [23]
